paragraphs: An adversarial patch can fool an object detector from one viewpoint yet lose effectiveness when viewed from another. This paper studies that problem for patches generated by text-to-image diffusion models. Its analysis finds that prompt wording substantially affects robustness across viewing angles, while task-specific written instructions fail to provide the desired improvement.

AngleRoCL addresses this by learning a concept represented through text embeddings: numerical representations that can be incorporated into prompts. The concept captures the ability to generate patches whose attacks withstand viewpoint changes. This makes angle robustness something the generation process is explicitly guided toward, rather than something requested only through ordinary language.

The authors evaluate the approach in simulations and physical experiments involving five detectors and multiple viewpoints. They report more than 50% average relative improvement in attack effectiveness across angles, with high success rates under challenging viewing conditions. These findings expose a practical detector vulnerability and show that learned textual concepts can influence physical properties of generated patches.
neurips-2025-anglerocl-angle-robust-conc.tldr: AngleRoCL learns prompt embeddings that help generated adversarial patches remain effective across physical viewing angles.

paragraphs: Robotic tasks often involve reaching several goals in a particular order while obeying safety requirements that change as the task progresses. Linear-time Temporal Logic provides a formal way to describe such requirements. The paper addresses the difficulty of learning these behaviors in continuous environments, where existing reinforcement learning methods for temporal specifications have shown poor empirical performance.

Automaton Constrained Q-Learning combines goal-conditioned value learning with guidance from an automaton representing the task. The automaton explicitly tracks stages of goal completion and encodes safety constraints, including constraints that vary over time. This gives the learning process a representation of both what should happen next and which restrictions apply at each stage. The method supports most LTL task specifications.

Across continuous control tasks, ACQL outperforms existing approaches, including settings where earlier methods fail at goal completion or safety. The authors also deploy it on a six-degree-of-freedom robotic arm navigating a cluttered, cabinet-like space. These results support its practical usefulness for learning behaviors governed by richer temporal requirements.
neurips-2025-automaton-constrained-q-lea.tldr: ACQL uses task automata to guide reinforcement learning through ordered robotic goals and changing safety constraints.

paragraphs: A CT scan is a volume whose fine anatomical details extend across many slices. Turning each slice into tokens separately can blur those relationships, while long scans create difficult sequence lengths. BTB3D focuses on improving this visual representation so that models can better connect three-dimensional anatomy with clinical language.

Its causal convolutional encoder-decoder supports both two-dimensional and three-dimensional processing and produces compact volumetric tokens that account for frequency information. Training proceeds through local reconstruction, overlapping windows, and refinement of the decoder over longer contexts. The authors report that learning from short slice excerpts generalizes to scans longer than 300 slices without additional memory overhead.

For report generation, BTB3D improves BLEU scores and raises clinical F1 by 40% over the named comparison systems. For text-to-CT generation, it reduces FID by 75% and halves FVD, producing anatomically consistent volumes at 512 by 512 by 241 resolution. The findings emphasize that preserving three-dimensional information in tokens is an essential component of scalable medical vision-language modeling.
neurips-2025-better-tokens-for-better-3d.tldr: BTB3D improves CT report generation and synthesis through compact tokens that preserve three-dimensional anatomical information.

paragraphs: Discrete prediction tasks are often trained using a smoother substitute objective, called a surrogate loss. A central question is whether optimizing that substitute leads to the right predictions for the original task. Calibration is a standard way to establish this connection, but checking it directly can be difficult. The paper investigates simpler conditions for convex, differentiable losses.

The first result concerns indirect elicitation, or IE. Under mild conditions, IE is equivalent to calibration for one-dimensional losses in this class. However, the authors construct a counterexample showing that the equivalence does not extend generally to higher dimensions. This makes dimensionality a substantive boundary for the simpler test.

The authors then introduce strong IE, a strengthened condition described as equally easy to verify. They prove that it implies calibration for differentiable surrogates. For strongly convex, differentiable surrogates, it is both necessary and sufficient. Applications across several problems demonstrate how these conditions can help researchers design and analyze consistent training objectives without always checking calibration directly.
neurips-2025-consistency-conditions-for-.tldr: The paper establishes simpler calibration tests for differentiable surrogate losses, with guarantees that depend on dimension and convexity.

paragraphs: Stereo image super-resolution improves the resolution of paired views of a scene. The two images provide related information, but combining it requires identifying useful correspondences. Transformer attention can also assign weight to irrelevant context, introducing noise that harms reconstructed details. DIFFSSR targets both this attention problem and difficulties caused by imperfect alignment between the views.

Its Diff Cross Attention Block separates relevant from irrelevant context, strengthening useful features while canceling attention noise. A second component, the Sliding Stereo Cross-Attention Module, combines sliding windows with attention based on disparity, the positional difference between corresponding content in the images. This allows feature integration to adapt to local variation.

The sliding mechanism also addresses performance degradation when corresponding image content does not align perfectly along horizontal epipolar lines. Experiments on benchmark datasets show better quantitative results and visual quality than comparison methods including NAFSSR and SwinFIRSSR. Together, the results support using selective attention and more adaptable stereo matching to improve reconstruction.
neurips-2025-diffssr-stereo-image-super-.tldr: DIFFSSR improves stereo super-resolution by suppressing attention noise and adapting cross-view matching to local misalignment.

paragraphs: Model-based reinforcement learning reduces the need for real environmental interactions by learning a world model that generates simulated experience. In visual environments, however, processing the whole observation together can obscure the moving objects and temporal changes that matter for rewards. DyMoDreamer introduces a mechanism intended to make these dynamics more explicit within the learned model.

The method constructs differential observations using a mask derived from differences between frames. These observations encode object motion and temporal information. Dynamic modulation is represented through stochastic categorical distributions and incorporated into a recurrent state-space model. This connects the motion-focused representation with the model's evolving internal description of the environment.

The reported experiments achieve a 156.6% mean human-normalized score on Atari 100k and a score of 832 on the DeepMind Visual Control Suite, described as new leading results. On Crafter, performance improves by 9.5% after one million steps. These findings support the value of explicitly extracting changing visual features when building world models for decision-making.
neurips-2025-dymodreamer-world-modeling-.tldr: DyMoDreamer improves visual reinforcement learning by incorporating explicit motion cues into its world model.

paragraphs: Bayesian optimization must choose promising evaluations while accounting for uncertainty about their rewards. This paper studies a further difficulty: the reward distribution itself may have an unknown or hard-to-specify form. Multiple modes, heavy tails, and changing distributions can undermine the modeling assumptions used by classical Gaussian-process approaches.

The proposed infinity-Gaussian Process uses a sequential spatial Dirichlet Process mixture with a Gaussian-process baseline. It represents uncertainty about both reward values and the model describing those values. Combined with Thompson sampling, this allows exploration and exploitation to account for competing distributional explanations, rather than relying on a single fixed distribution type.

The authors prove that the surrogate can approximate a broad class of reward distributions and establish near-minimax-optimal posterior contraction rates, describing how its uncertainty concentrates as evidence accumulates. Experiments show improvements over leading approaches in challenging settings, including strongly non-stationary and heavy-tailed rewards. The contribution is therefore both a more flexible reward model and a way to use its model uncertainty when choosing evaluations.
neurips-2025-exploring-and-exploiting-mo.tldr: The infinity-Gaussian Process helps Bayesian optimization account for uncertainty about the reward distribution as well as reward values.

paragraphs: Long-range video synthesis requires a model to generate new content while maintaining motion and meaning across successive frames. GPDiT combines autoregressive modeling, which predicts future frames from earlier context, with diffusion-based learning. It carries out this process in a continuous latent space, where frames have numerical representations rather than discrete token identities.

The model predicts future latent frames autoregressively using a diffusion loss. This connects sequential prediction with a training objective suited to continuous generation, supporting motion dynamics and semantic consistency. The authors also introduce a lightweight causal attention mechanism and time conditioning based on rotations that adds no parameters. Both changes are intended to improve training and inference efficiency.

Experiments report strong results in video generation, video representation, and learning from few examples. The representation findings matter because they indicate that the framework learns useful video features alongside its generative ability. Taken together, the results support continuous autoregressive diffusion as a promising framework for video modeling across generation and representation tasks.
neurips-2025-generative-pre-trained-auto.tldr: GPDiT combines autoregressive frame prediction with diffusion learning in continuous latent space for video generation and representation.

paragraphs: A greedy bandit algorithm repeatedly chooses the action that currently looks best, without deliberately exploring alternatives. Whether that works depends on what the observed rewards reveal about the available choices. This paper studies the question for arbitrary finite, known reward structures, extending beyond the specific structures considered in earlier work.

The main result identifies partial identifiability as a necessary and sufficient condition for the greedy algorithm's asymptotic success. Success means sublinear regret: accumulated loss relative to optimal choices grows more slowly than time. Failure means linear regret. The characterization therefore gives a precise boundary between instances where exploitation alone eventually succeeds and instances where it does not.

A stronger consequence is that, when the property holds, any algorithm satisfying a mild non-degeneracy condition achieves success in the same asymptotic sense. The favorable structure of the instance is thus central to the guarantee. The authors extend their characterization to contextual bandits and interactive decision-making with arbitrary feedback, and provide examples and extensions involving infinite reward structures.
neurips-2025-greedy-algorithms-for-struc.tldr: Partial identifiability exactly characterizes when greedy learning achieves sublinear rather than linear regret in finite structured bandits.

paragraphs: A small visual edit can change an image's meaning even when most of the picture stays the same. Multimodal language models may overlook such changes or describe differences that are absent. This paper addresses the problem through both targeted training examples and a learning objective aimed at improving fine-grained visual understanding.

The authors build a controlled generation pipeline that creates minimally edited image pairs with corresponding captions. Their Micro Edit Dataset contains more than 50,000 image-text pairs across 11 categories, including changes in attributes, counts, positions, and object presence. Supervised fine-tuning adds a feature-level consistency loss that encourages stable visual embeddings under small edits.

Evaluation uses carefully balanced image pairs in the Micro Edit Detection benchmark. The approach improves difference detection and reduces hallucinations relative to strong baselines, including GPT-4o. It also produces consistent gains in image captioning and visual question answering. These findings suggest that learning from controlled visual changes can improve broader vision-language behavior as well as sensitivity to subtle edits.
neurips-2025-hallucination-at-a-glance-c.tldr: Controlled image edits and a consistency-based training objective improve subtle visual difference detection and reduce multimodal hallucinations.

paragraphs: Video language models spend substantial computation processing redundant visual tokens. Removing tokens inside the language model still incurs costs in its early layers, while earlier removal methods often consider individual frames or short time windows. HoliTom combines reduction before and within the model, accounting for correlations across longer video sequences.

Before the language model, HoliTom segments the video using global temporal redundancy and then merges information across space and time. This reduces visual token counts by more than 90%. Inside the language model, it applies a further similarity-based merging procedure designed to work well with the earlier reduction. The complete framework requires no training.

On LLaVA-OneVision-7B, the method retains 99.1% of the original performance while using 6.9% of the original floating-point operations. It also reports a 2.28-fold reduction in time to the first token and 1.32-fold higher decoding throughput. These measurements show practical latency benefits alongside reduced computation, supporting the combined treatment of redundancy at both stages.
neurips-2025-holitom-holistic-token-merg.tldr: HoliTom merges redundant video tokens before and inside the language model, substantially reducing computation while retaining nearly all measured performance.

paragraphs: Hypergraphs represent relationships involving groups of nodes, allowing learning systems to describe interactions beyond pairs. Passing information repeatedly through these groups can make node representations too similar, a problem called over-smoothing. The paper develops a message-passing framework inspired by interacting particles, with hyperedges acting as fields that influence shared node dynamics.

The dynamics combine attraction, repulsion, and Allen-Cahn forcing terms to produce class-dependent equilibria that help keep representations separable. The authors investigate both first-order and second-order systems, finding the second-order formulation more stable and suitable for deeper propagation. They also introduce stochasticity to represent uncertainty in interactions rather than treating every exchange as deterministic.

The theoretical analysis establishes a positive lower bound on hypergraph Dirichlet energy during propagation, supporting the claim that the method resists over-smoothing. Empirical node-classification results are competitive across real-world datasets, including those connecting similar classes and those connecting different classes. Together, the analysis and experiments connect particle dynamics with deeper hypergraph learning that preserves useful distinctions between nodes.
neurips-2025-how-particle-system-theory-.tldr: Particle-inspired hypergraph dynamics preserve distinctions between node representations and support deeper message passing.

paragraphs: Neural scene reconstruction can struggle when photographs of the same environment have very different exposures. Scenes containing windows or both indoor and outdoor areas are especially challenging because brightness varies strongly. These differences can degrade synthesized views even when reconstruction methods perform well on carefully curated captures.

Neural Exposure Fields address the problem by learning an exposure value for each three-dimensional point. A neural conditioning mechanism allows the exposure field and scene representation to be optimized jointly. Exposure is therefore tied to scene locations in three dimensions, helping the reconstructed appearance remain consistent as the viewpoint changes. The approach supports high-dynamic-range scenes without requiring multi-exposure captures or post-processing.

The authors report superior results on challenging real-world data, faster training than prior work, and improvements exceeding 55% over the best-performing baselines on several benchmarks. These findings support treating exposure as part of the learned scene itself. The contribution is a representation and optimization strategy for handling capture variation while maintaining coherent appearance across generated views.
neurips-2025-learning-neural-exposure-fi.tldr: Neural Exposure Fields jointly learn three-dimensional exposure and scene appearance to improve view synthesis from unevenly exposed captures.

paragraphs: In long-tailed recognition, a few classes have many training examples while numerous other classes have few. This imbalance makes generalization especially difficult for rare classes, including when fine-tuning foundation models. The paper investigates how the allocation of model capacity contributes to the problem and proposes changing the model's parameter space directly.

Model Rebalancing, or MORE, introduces a low-rank parameter component that mediates how capacity is allocated. A tailored loss and sinusoidal reweighting schedule guide this adjustment. The framework is designed to achieve the rebalancing without increasing overall model complexity or inference costs, making its effect relevant to both recognition quality and deployment efficiency.

Experiments cover multiple long-tailed benchmarks with both multi-class and multi-label tasks. MORE significantly improves generalization, particularly for rare classes, and also complements existing imbalance remedies. This combination matters because it identifies parameter allocation as another useful intervention alongside changes to data or training losses. The reported breadth of results supports its potential as a reusable module for imbalanced recognition.
neurips-2025-long-tailed-recognition-wit.tldr: MORE improves recognition of rare classes by rebalancing model parameters without increasing overall complexity or inference cost.

paragraphs: Temporal graph learning uses evolving networks to predict future interactions. Most existing work trains on a single network, leaving open how well learned patterns transfer to other networks within or across domains. This paper introduces both a larger evaluation setting and a pretraining framework aimed at learning temporal dynamics that transfer.

The benchmark contains 84 real-world temporal transaction networks. The Temporal Multi-network Transfer framework, called MiNT, is trained on as many as 64 networks and evaluated on 20 held-out networks. Testing on unseen networks makes generalization across networks a central part of the evaluation, rather than measuring only predictions within the network used for training.

MiNT consistently outperforms models trained individually, and transfer performance has a strong relationship with the number of pretraining networks. The authors interpret these results as evidence of scaling trends and the importance of network diversity. The work provides a foundation for studying temporal graph foundation models by making multi-network training and transfer measurable at a larger scale.
neurips-2025-mint-multi-network-transfer.tldr: MiNT introduces an 84-network benchmark and shows that multi-network pretraining improves temporal graph transfer to unseen networks.

paragraphs: Predicting molecular properties supports drug discovery and materials research. Language-model approaches often describe molecules through text formats such as SMILES or SELFIES, which the authors argue can leave structural information unclear. MolVision investigates whether combining molecular structure images with textual descriptions improves the information available for property prediction.

The study constructs a benchmark spanning nine datasets and both classification and numerical prediction tasks. It evaluates nine vision-language models with no task examples, a few examples, and task-specific fine-tuning. This setup examines the role of visual information across several levels of adaptation, rather than judging it in only one training setting.

The results show that images improve prediction, especially alongside efficient fine-tuning with LoRA. Visual input alone is insufficient in the evaluated setting, while combining images and text significantly improves generalization across molecular properties. Adapting the vision encoder to molecular images together with LoRA brings further gains. The findings support multimodal fusion and domain adaptation as complementary components of molecular prediction.
neurips-2025-molvision-molecular-propert.tldr: MolVision finds that combining molecular images and text, especially with targeted adaptation, improves molecular property prediction.

paragraphs: Several analyses of neural-network training rely on a property called non-singularity of the gradient descent map. Here, this means that the preimage of a measure-zero set also has measure zero. The property has been used in results about avoiding saddles and maxima and in characterizations of convergence to global minima.

Previous work often assumes non-singularity or obtains it using restrictive smoothness conditions and small step sizes. This paper studies neural networks as functions of their weights and biases and proves the property for realistic architectures containing fully connected, convolutional, or softmax attention layers. Its activation class includes piecewise analytic functions such as ReLU, leaky ReLU, and sigmoid.

The guarantee holds for almost all step sizes, extending the scope beyond analyses restricted to small steps. This supplies a previously assumed ingredient for convergence results in more practical neural-network settings. The result establishes a structural property of the update map; its significance lies in broadening the applicability of existing analyses of gradient descent and stochastic gradient descent.
neurips-2025-non-singularity-of-the-grad.tldr: The paper proves gradient descent map non-singularity for practical neural architectures with piecewise analytic activations at almost all step sizes.

paragraphs: A model can be good at solving a complete problem yet struggle to recognize which missing fact would make an incomplete problem solvable. QuestBench isolates this information-gathering ability. It represents underspecified reasoning as a constraint satisfaction problem with missing variable assignments, focusing on a special case with one necessary assignment missing.

The benchmark contains logic problems, planning tasks with partially observed starting states, grade-school mathematics, and equation-based versions of those mathematics problems. Each task can be resolved by asking at most one question. Models select the appropriate clarification from multiple options, allowing the evaluation to focus on identifying the necessary information.

Current models perform strongly on the mathematics variants but reach only 40–50% accuracy on the logic and planning tasks. Further analysis shows failures even when a model can solve the corresponding fully specified problem. The findings distinguish reasoning with available facts from choosing which fact to acquire and motivate training specifically for information acquisition.
neurips-2025-questbench-can-llms-ask-the.tldr: QuestBench shows that solving complete reasoning problems does not ensure an LLM can identify the right clarification question.

paragraphs: Bilevel optimization places one optimization problem inside another. The upper-level objective may depend on choosing among several lower-level solutions, producing a hyper-objective that can be nonsmooth. Because finding global optima is generally intractable, researchers seek stationary points. Existing guarantees often use weaker stationarity notions or restrictive assumptions that make the hyper-objective smooth.

The paper introduces set smoothness, a property describing how the lower-level solution set varies with the upper-level variable. The authors prove it holds for a broad class of problems. It ensures weak convexity for pessimistic hyper-objectives and weak concavity for optimistic ones, providing useful structure even when ordinary smoothness is absent.

Using this structure, the authors establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for a zeroth-order algorithm computing approximate Clarke hyper-stationary points. This supplies a stronger stationarity guarantee in the nonsmooth setting without the earlier smoothness requirements. The authors describe it as the first computational guarantee of this kind and suggest that set smoothness could also inform broader optimization and variational analysis.
neurips-2025-set-smoothness-unlocks-clar.tldr: Set smoothness enables guaranteed computation of approximate Clarke hyper-stationary points for a broad class of nonsmooth bilevel problems.

paragraphs: Spatial studies often need to estimate how a covariate is associated with an outcome, including the sign and magnitude of that association. Accurate prediction alone does not answer this question. The paper shows that existing uncertainty intervals can miss their intended coverage when models are misspecified and observation locations are nonrandom, both common features of spatial data.

The proposed method builds frequentist confidence intervals using a form of spatial smoothness and Gaussian errors with constant variance. It does not require the fitted model to be correct or require covariate overlap between training and target locations. These features directly address obstacles to interpreting associations across different spatial samples.

When the Gaussian noise variance is known, the intervals have valid finite-sample coverage under the stated assumptions. When it is unknown, the authors provide an asymptotically consistent variance estimator. Real and simulated experiments outperform existing techniques. The central contribution is an uncertainty guarantee for spatial associations with explicit assumptions, rather than relying on predictive accuracy as evidence that estimated relationships are reliable.
neurips-2025-smooth-sailing-lipschitz-dr.tldr: The method provides confidence intervals for spatial associations under smoothness and constant-variance Gaussian error assumptions, without requiring model correctness.

paragraphs: Text-to-SQL systems let people ask database questions in ordinary language. A generated query can be valid SQL while still expressing the wrong meaning, making successful execution an incomplete indication of reliability. SQLens addresses this gap by detecting semantic errors in generated queries and using the resulting evidence to guide corrections.

The framework combines error signals from the underlying database with signals from the language model. It uses them to identify possible problems within individual SQL clauses, giving the diagnosis finer granularity than a single judgment about the whole query. Those same signals then inform the correction process, connecting error localization with repair.

On two public benchmarks, SQLens improves error-detection F1 by 25.78% relative to the best language-model self-evaluation method and raises execution accuracy of out-of-the-box text-to-SQL systems by up to 20%. The findings support checking generated queries with both database and model evidence. They also show that detecting meaning-level errors can lead to improvements in the queries ultimately executed.
neurips-2025-sqlens-an-end-to-end-framew.tldr: SQLens combines database and language-model signals to detect clause-level semantic errors and improve generated SQL queries.

paragraphs: Tracking a point through video is complicated by the fact that both the scene and the camera may move. TAPIP3D builds a three-dimensional representation that compensates for camera motion. It uses depth and camera-motion information to lift image features into a shared world space, supporting long-term tracking in monocular RGB and RGB-D videos.

Within this stabilized representation, the model repeatedly refines motion estimates across multiple frames. Its Neighborhood-to-Neighborhood attention constructs spatially coherent neighborhoods suited to irregular three-dimensional point distributions. This replaces the conventional square image windows used for matching in earlier trackers with a mechanism organized around three-dimensional geometry.

Experiments show substantial robustness gains from compensating for camera motion and strong results across several 3D tracking benchmarks. TAPIP3D improves over existing 3D methods and also exceeds leading 2D pixel trackers in accuracy when reliable depth is available. It supports both camera-centered and world-centered coordinates, while the reported comparison highlights the value of stabilizing the representation.
neurips-2025-tapip3d-tracking-any-point-.tldr: TAPIP3D improves long-term point tracking through camera-stabilized 3D features and geometry-aware neighborhood attention.

paragraphs: Time series can be accompanied by text that helps explain the system being observed. TimeXL uses that context together with numerical observations to produce predictions and explanations. Its starting point is a prototype-based encoder that processes both modalities and generates preliminary forecasts with case-based rationales, connecting predictions to representative patterns.

Three language models then take distinct roles in a feedback loop. A prediction model reasons over the encoder's forecasts and explanations to refine the output. A reflection model compares predictions with ground truth and identifies inconsistent or noisy text. A refinement model uses that feedback to improve the text and trigger another round of encoder training.

Evaluations on four real-world datasets report improvements of up to 8.9% in AUC and explanations that combine temporal and textual information. The approach makes contextual text an input that can be revised through feedback, alongside refining predictions. Its stated gains support integrating prediction, critique, and text refinement within an explainable multimodal time-series framework.
neurips-2025-timexl-explainable-multi-mo.tldr: TimeXL combines prototype-based time-series modeling with three language models that refine forecasts, critique errors, and improve contextual text.

paragraphs: Anomaly detectors trained only on normal examples often identify unusual inputs through reconstruction error. This can fail when the model also reconstructs abnormal examples well. The paper proposes a framework that directs reconstructions toward the normal-data manifold, the region representing normal samples, so abnormal inputs become less faithfully reconstructed.

The approach uses a contraction mapping whose repeated application converges to a fixed point. The authors use normal-only training to place that fixed point within the normal manifold. Iterating the mapping then moves abnormal inputs toward normal structure, increasing their discrepancy from the original input. This gives reconstruction an explicit directional constraint.

The framework also uses its invertible mapping for flow-based density estimation, with a prior learned from the preceding reconstruction to estimate input likelihood. A bidirectional architecture combines forward reconstruction with backward density estimation, supplying two complementary anomaly signals. Experiments on tabular data, natural images, and industrial images demonstrate the method's effectiveness across these data types.
neurips-2025-unifying-reconstruction-and.tldr: The framework combines contraction-guided reconstruction and density estimation to detect anomalies using training data containing only normal examples.

paragraphs: In-context learning lets a model change its behavior through the context it receives. For function approximation, that context can act as a control input. This paper studies the practical restriction that context consists of tokens selected from a finite vocabulary, calling the resulting setting vocabulary in-context learning.

The authors ask whether single-layer Transformers in this setting have the universal approximation property: the ability to approximate functions arbitrarily closely in the theoretical setting under consideration. They show that, without positional encoding, vocabulary in-context learning lacks this property. This identifies an expressive limitation of the architecture when context is restricted to finite-vocabulary tokens.

Adding positional encoding makes universal approximation possible, and the paper gives several sufficient conditions on the encoding. The result does not say that every positional encoding works; the conditions establish ways to obtain the property. The contribution gives an approximation-theoretic explanation for the value of position information in in-context learning, connecting an architectural choice to what a shallow Transformer can represent.
neurips-2025-vocabulary-in-context-learn.tldr: Suitable positional encodings enable universal approximation through finite-vocabulary context in single-layer Transformers, where it is impossible without them.
